calls.reason: No transcript or recording of Musk's FII8 session was found. Fortune confirms the 10x claim but says nothing about whether he mentioned data, compute or LLM limits.
Reuters documents Musk's repeated missed self-driving deadlines, which supports the track-record part. But the humanoid prediction it calls overoptimistic runs to 2040 and is unresolved.
DeSmog shows Dominion kept a coal plant open citing data-centre demand, which partly supports the fossil-fuel point. Nothing links AI power demand to gains for oil-rich countries.
Two days before the deadline, the CAIS Remote Labor Index shows the best AI automating only 15.8% of real remote projects at professional quality. AI is nowhere near doing anything a human can do.

Omdia counts about 13,000 humanoid-type robots shipped in 2025 and 2,300 in 2024. That is roughly six orders of magnitude short of the ~10 billion threshold, so near-term sales at that scale are effectively ruled out.

Omdia's ~13,000 units in 2025 is negligible next to the roughly 9 billion humanoids that six per car would need. Altman Solon finds 69% of US consumers won't pay over $5,000, a real affordability barrier.
